content: This is the chapter that opens on the Mongolia shaman night — the July 18, 2011 field notes, Burkhan Khaldun. If that scene is already in the book, is it worth one line here connecting back to it? Right now a reader who remembers that night gets nothing that rewards it.
author: Claude
quote: We had even begun writing something together, a chapter we called The Enigma of Mind: A Theory of Evolution and Conscious Experience.

content: This call is where the belonging wound actually resolves — it's the emotional hinge of the chapter — but it's the most summarized passage here, in a book that's otherwise very good at scene. One concrete detail (where you were sitting, what changed in his voice) might let the reader feel the shift instead of being told about it.
author: Claude
quote: He wasn't advising from above. He was listening the way a colleague listens, leaning in, asking questions, making connections I hadn't seen.

content: This completes the door image from Ch13's Andes cave — image, then body, now word. Strong as a callback. Just flagging in case it's meant to stand on its own instead — worth a deliberate check either way.
author: Claude
quote: We have built our cultures in the shape of doors.
